summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships a postinstall hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and a top-level `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` call in index.js that POST a JSON body containing the installer's hostname, install path, current working directory, Node.js version and package name to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The destination is not associated with the declared publisher scope and the payload is framed in source comments as 'build-provenance'. The package body itself is a no-op Proxy shim with no functional API — every exported property returns a stub — so the beacon is the artifact's only effect. The combination of a generic scoped name, version 99.0.2 (an implausibly high version used to win internal resolution), empty functionality, and an install- and import-time callback to an attacker-controlled bare IP is the dependency-confusion / reconnaissance beacon shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
